chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Gibson's party mixes players; Roy Haynes
summary: Dance and Gus talk about unhappy players mixed with unsuited drummers like Roy Haynes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, about Dick -- it's interesting to talk about that party a little bit. I know a lot of guys would get upset by where they'd find themselves -- the position they'd find themselves in, who they're backing up.
Like what?
Well, there was a great big mixture, very often.
Well, sure. He just tried to mix everybody up with everybody.
Well, some guys don't feel very comfortable, right?
That's right, that's true, that's true.
And you take a real modern drummer or something --
That's right.
-- and stick them up there.
That happened. The year before last he had a very modern drummer there, and a lot of them didn't want to play with him, because --

If it's all right with you, as I say, this isn't going anywhere, but -- well, the last time I was out I guess he had Roy Haynes and he had -- right? That's what I thought, because I saw it all happen, and I saw a lot of unhappy faces on the stand.
Yeah, he played a little bit too much behind them.
Yeah, that's right.
They were used to this, and what Roy Haynes plays, he's great in his style of playing.
A lot of guys want a guy just like Roy Haines, but a lot of guys are --
Most of the guys want somebody who's going to be just -- right there.
That's not interfering.
Yeah, interfering with them. You were there for that, then?
Yes, I was there.
Oh, yeah.
I saw that. That's why I'm asking you that question, because I saw a couple of -- I saw Red Callender and (unintelligible) up on the band, and a lot of very unhappy faces.
Sure.
Which is very understandable, and to me and to Stannie, we're thinking, now, how come Dick would do this?
Well, he had to put him somewhere.
Well, he evidently likes to do it, though, huh, Gus?
Well, not exactly. He don't want to -- he was trying to bring something different to the people, truthfully.
Yeah.
That's the way --
And he also -- maybe he thinks that by doing something unorthodox like that, something unexpected may come out of it. Maybe he thinks that?
Well, not exactly. But he was just trying to -- his way of thinking is to try and fit somebody with this one and that one, to mix them up.
